routes.name: Visa-free short stay (Schengen)
routes.summary: Citizens of many countries can visit Greece without a visa. The Greek foreign ministry publishes the full list. Stay is up to 90 days in any 180 days.

other: Biometric passport required for Albania, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Georgia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia and Ukraine.
Check the official list for your passport.

sources.label: Greece MFA: countries requiring or not requiring a visa

routes.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C)
routes.summary: Travelers from countries not on the visa-free list need a Schengen visa. Apply through a Greek mission in your country.

other: Fee, processing time and document list not confirmed on a reachable official page. Check the Greek mission handling your application.

sources.label: Greece MFA: countries requiring or not requiring a visa

routes.name: Financially Independent Person Residence Permit (Article 20)
routes.summary: Residence for non-EU people with steady income who will not work in Greece, for example retirees. The permit is valid for 2 years.

income.note: Add 20% for a spouse and 15% per child. The official page calls it stable annual income but lists a monthly figure.

other: Needs a Type D entry visa and a private health insurance policy.
No employment in Greece.
Proof of funds is mainly a foreign pension or a Greek bank statement.

sources.label: Attica Decentralized Administration: financially independent, issuance

routes.name: Golden Visa (Real Estate Investment, Article 16A)
routes.summary: Residence permit for non-EU buyers of Greek property. Minimum is EUR 800,000 in Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and islands over 3,100 residents, and EUR 400,000 elsewhere.

investment.note: Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and islands with over 3,100 residents. EUR 400,000 in all other areas. Raised under Law 5100/2024, Art. 64.

other: Permit length and other property rules not stated on the pages read. The Migration Ministry golden visa page still mentions an older EUR 250,000 figure, so check current rules before applying.

sources.label: Housing portal: golden visa threshold increase

routes.name: Investor Residence Categories (Investment Activity, Strategic, Securities and Deposits)
routes.summary: Greece lists investor residence permits for investment activity (Art. 16A), strategic investors (Art. 16B) and securities or bank deposits (Art. 16C). The official page gives no amounts.

other: Amounts and conditions are not on the category page. Check the Migration Ministry before relying on this.

routes.name: Employment Residence Permit (Dependent Work)
routes.summary: Residence permit for non-EU workers in dependent employment, listed under Article 15. Conditions, duration and fees are not on the category page.

other: Conditions, duration and fees not confirmed. Check the Migration Ministry.

routes.name: Special-Purpose Worker and Intra-Company Transfer Permits
routes.summary: Permits for directors and board members, specialized and technical staff, athletes and coaches, creators, clergy, foreign press correspondents and teachers at foreign schools. Intra-company transfers are listed as a separate category.

other: Conditions not confirmed. See the official category list.

routes.name: EU Blue Card
routes.summary: EU Blue Card for highly skilled non-EU workers, listed under Article 114 of Law 4251/2014, with intra-EU mobility under Article 122.

other: Salary threshold, degree rules and duration not confirmed on an official page.

routes.name: Student Residence Permit (Article 33)
routes.summary: Residence permit for study, listed under Article 33, with student mobility under Article 35. Researcher and vocational training permits are separate categories.

other: Requirements, fees and work hours not confirmed on an official page.

routes.name: Family Reunification (Family of Non-EU Residents)
routes.summary: Family members of non-EU residents can get permits. Greece lists entry approval, family members (Art. 72) and families formed in Greece (Art. 80).

other: Income, waiting time and age rules not confirmed.

routes.name: Family of a Greek or EU Citizen
routes.summary: Spouses, partners, descendants, parents and other dependent relatives of Greek or EU citizens have their own permit categories, including permanent residence for family of Greek citizens (Art. 83).

other: Conditions not read on an official page. Based on the Migration Ministry category list.

routes.name: Asylum and Humanitarian Residence
routes.summary: Greece lists humanitarian residence for trafficking victims, domestic violence and crime victims, abusive working conditions, serious health conditions and more. Use the official process.

other: Use the official process only. Details not summarized here.

sources.label: Migration Ministry guide for international protection beneficiaries

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss Free Movement
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens can move freely in Greece. Family of EU citizens have their own permit categories.

other: Registration rules not confirmed.

routes.name: Long-Term Resident Status
routes.summary: Long-term residence for non-EU nationals, plus a second-generation permit. Years and income needed are not on the category page.

other: Years of residence and income requirements not confirmed on an official page.

routes.name: Naturalization (General Route)
routes.summary: Non-EU nationals can apply after 7 years of legal residence. Refugees and stateless people need 3. EU citizens need 3. Parents of an underage Greek citizen, and spouses of Greeks with a child together, also need 3.

other: Fee EUR 700 first application, EUR 200 for later ones. Refugees and stateless EUR 100. EU citizens EUR 100.
The guide does not mention a knowledge test or dual citizenship rules.

routes.name: Citizenship by Marriage or Parenthood of a Greek Child
routes.summary: Non-EU spouses of a Greek citizen with a child together, or parents of an underage Greek citizen, can apply after 3 years of residence. Marriage alone does not shorten the 7 years.

other: Parent route does not apply if the child became Greek through attending a Greek school.

routes.name: Citizenship by Descent (Greek Origin)
routes.summary: People with a Greek citizen ancestor, or a co-ethnic ancestor, can apply through a Greek embassy or consulate. Fees are EUR 100 for descendants of a Greek citizen and EUR 120 for descendants of a co-ethnic.

other: Generations not stated in the guide. You need documents proving the relationship.
Co-ethnics from Albania, Turkey and ex-USSR with a special ID card must live permanently in Greece.

routes.processing: 18 months for the Greek citizen ancestor route, per the guide.

routes.name: Citizenship by Birth in Greece or Greek Schooling
routes.summary: Children born in Greece can apply after enrolling in first grade of elementary school, within the guide's limits on how long the parents lived in Greece before the birth.

other: Parent residence limits apply: more than 5 years before the birth or more than 10 years in total. Read the guide for details.
